553: static int sdio_recvsetup(FAR struct sdio_dev_s *dev, FAR uint8_t *buffer,
554:                           size_t nbytes)
555: {
556:   FAR struct bk7258_sdio_s *priv = (FAR struct bk7258_sdio_s *)dev;
557:   uint32_t value;
558: 
559:   if (buffer == NULL || nbytes == 0 || priv->blocklen == 0 ||
560:       priv->nblocks == 0 || nbytes != (priv->blocklen * priv->nblocks))
561:     {
562:       return -EINVAL;
563:     }
564: 
565:   /* Match the vendor read setup order: program timeout and clear stale W1C
566:    * status before asserting the RX FIFO and SD state resets. */
567:   sdio_write(BK7258_SDIO_DATA_TIMER, BK7258_SDIO_TIMEOUT);
568:   sdio_write(BK7258_SDIO_INT_STATUS, 0xffffffffu);
569:   while (nxsem_trywait(&priv->data_sem) == OK)
570:     {
571:     }
572: 
573:   /* Complete the vendor V2 reset pulse before configuring the receive
574:    * transaction. */
575:   value = sdio_read(BK7258_SDIO_FIFO);
576:   value &= ~(0xffffu | BK7258_SDIO_FIFO_RX_RESET |
577:              BK7258_SDIO_FIFO_TX_RESET | BK7258_SDIO_STATE_RESET);
578:   sdio_write(BK7258_SDIO_FIFO, value);
579: 
580:   value |= 0x0101u | BK7258_SDIO_FIFO_RX_RESET |
581:            BK7258_SDIO_STATE_RESET | BK7258_SDIO_CLOCK_RECOVERY;
582:   sdio_write(BK7258_SDIO_FIFO, value);
583: 
584:   value = ((priv->blocklen << BK7258_SDIO_DATA_BLOCK_SHIFT) &
585:            BK7258_SDIO_DATA_BLOCK_MASK) | BK7258_SDIO_DATA_BYTE_SELECT;
586:   /* BK7258 V2 uses its multi-block data engine for 512-byte reads even when
587:    * the card command is CMD17. Short register transfers such as SCR remain
588:    * in single-block mode. */
589: 
590:   if (priv->blocklen == 512)
591:     {
592:       value |= BK7258_SDIO_DATA_MULTIBLOCK;
593:     }
594:   /* Keep configuration and start as separate writes, matching the vendor
595:    * set_read_multi_block_data()/start_receive_data() sequence. */
596:   priv->buffer = buffer;
597:   priv->remaining = nbytes;
598:   priv->irq_status = 0;
599:   priv->data_result = -EINPROGRESS;
600:   priv->data_active = true;
601:   priv->data_write = false;
602:   sdio_write(BK7258_SDIO_DATA_CTRL, value);
603:   modifyreg32(BK7258_SDIO_INT_MASK, 0,
604:               BK7258_SDIO_DATA_RECEIVE_END |
605:               BK7258_SDIO_DATA_TIMEOUT);
606:   sdio_write(BK7258_SDIO_DATA_CTRL, value | BK7258_SDIO_DATA_ENABLE);
607: 
608:   /* The vendor card driver requires this settling interval after starting
609:    * the receive engine; without it the receive-end event can be missed. */
610: 
611:   nxsig_usleep(2000);
612:   return OK;
613: }

719:   while (priv->remaining != 0)
720:     {
721:       uint32_t word;
722:       unsigned int timeout = 400;

724:                     sizeof(word);

726:       while ((sdio_read(BK7258_SDIO_FIFO) & BK7258_SDIO_RX_READY) == 0 &&
727:              timeout-- != 0)

187: 			 << SDCARD_FIFO_TX_FIFO_THRESHOLD_POSI);

238: SDIO_Error sdio_wait_cmd_response(UINT32 cmd)
239: {
240: 	UINT32 reg;
241: #if (CONFIG_SOC_BK7256XX)
242: 	uint32_t i_timeout = 0x1000000;
243: #endif
244: 
245: 	while (1) {
246: 		reg = REG_READ(REG_SDCARD_CMD_RSP_INT_SEL);
247: 		//wait until cmd response
248: 		if (reg & (SDCARD_CMDRSP_NORSP_END_INT
249: 				   | SDCARD_CMDRSP_RSP_END_INT
250: 				   | SDCARD_CMDRSP_TIMEOUT_INT))
251: 			break;
252: 
253: #if (CONFIG_SOC_BK7256XX)
254: 		i_timeout--;
255: 		if(i_timeout == 0)
256: 		{
257: 			SDCARD_WARN("%s:cmd%d fatal err:no resp/end/timeout int\r\n", __func__, cmd);
258: 			return SD_CMD_RSP_TIMEOUT;
259: 		}
260: #endif
261: 	}
262: 
263: 	REG_WRITE(REG_SDCARD_CMD_RSP_INT_SEL, SD_CMD_RSP);//clear the int flag
264: 	if ((reg & SDCARD_CMDRSP_TIMEOUT_INT) /*||(reg&SDCARD_CMDRSP_NORSP_END_INT)*/) {
265: 		if ((cmd != 1))
266: 			SDCARD_WARN("sdcard cmd %d timeout,cmdresp_int_reg:0x%x\r\n", cmd, reg);
267: 		return SD_CMD_RSP_TIMEOUT;
268: 	}
269: 	if (reg & SDCARD_CMDRSP_CMD_CRC_FAIL) {
270: 
271: 		if ((cmd != 41) && (cmd != 2) && (cmd != 9) && (cmd != 1)) {
272: 			SDCARD_WARN("sdcard cmd %d crcfail,cmdresp_int_reg:0x%x\r\n", cmd, reg);
273: 			return SD_CMD_CRC_FAIL;
274: 		}
275: 	}
276: 
277: 	//os_printf("%s cmd=%d\r\n", __func__, cmd);
278: 
279: 	return SD_OK;
280: }

341: SDIO_Error sdcard_wait_receive_data(UINT8 *receive_buf)
342: {
343: 	#define WAIT_MAX_CNT (0x1000000)	//Temp code
344: 	UINT32 reg, i = 0;
345: 
346: 	while (1) {
347: 		reg = REG_READ(REG_SDCARD_CMD_RSP_INT_SEL);
348: 		if (reg & (SDCARD_CMDRSP_DATA_REC_END_INT
349: 				   | SDCARD_CMDRSP_DATA_CRC_FAIL
350: 				   | SDCARD_CMDRSP_DATA_TIME_OUT_INT))
351: 			break;
352: 
353: 		//Temp code
354: 		i++;
355: 		if((i >= WAIT_MAX_CNT) && (i % 0x100000 == 0))
356: 			SDCARD_PRT("%s:i=%x,timeout\r\n", __func__, i);
357: 	}
358: 
359: 	REG_WRITE(REG_SDCARD_CMD_RSP_INT_SEL, SD_DATA_RSP);//clear the int flag
360: 	if (reg & SDCARD_CMDRSP_DATA_TIME_OUT_INT)
361: 		return SD_DATA_TIMEOUT;
362: 	if (reg & SDCARD_CMDRSP_DATA_CRC_FAIL) {
363: 		SDCARD_WARN("sdcard data crcfail,cmdresp_int_reg:0x%x\r\n", reg);
364: 		return SD_DATA_CRC_FAIL;
365: 	}
366: 
367: 	for (i = 0; i < SD_DEFAULT_BLOCK_SIZE ;) {
368: 		/* wait fifo data valid */
369: 		while (1) {
370: 			//software  needn't handle dead-loop,hardware can garantee
371: 			if (REG_READ(REG_SDCARD_FIFO_THRESHOLD)&SDCARD_FIFO_RXFIFO_RD_READY)
372: 				break;
373: 		}
374: 		reg = REG_READ(REG_SDCARD_RD_DATA_ADDR);
375: 		*(receive_buf + i++) = reg & 0xff;
376: 		*(receive_buf + i++) = (reg >> 8) & 0xff;
377: 		*(receive_buf + i++) = (reg >> 16) & 0xff;
378: 		*(receive_buf + i++) = (reg >> 24) & 0xff;
379: 	}
380: 
381: 	return SD_OK;
382: }

**Blocking Findings**
Blocking findings are present. Items 1 through 4 should be resolved before treating the writable storage path as safe.

1. **Critical: TX FIFO timeout underflows and continues writing to a non-ready FIFO.**  
   [bk7258_sdio.c:195](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_sdio.c:195) uses `timeout-- != 0`. When the final poll still finds `TX_READY` clear, the comparison returns false but decrements unsigned `timeout` from zero to `UINT_MAX`. Consequently, the check at [bk7258_sdio.c:202](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_sdio.c:202) does not report `-ETIMEDOUT`; the code writes the word and consumes the buffer at [bk7258_sdio.c:207](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_sdio.c:207). A stalled or full FIFO can therefore silently drop/corrupt a sector while `remaining` reaches zero and the transfer appears complete.

2. **High: the advertised CMD24-only path programs the host as a multi-block data transfer.**  
   Both delivered configurations force single-block MMCSD operations with `CONFIG_MMCSD_MULTIBLOCK_LIMIT=1` at [ai_agent/defconfig:87](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/configs/ai_agent/defconfig:87) and [nsh/defconfig:86](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/configs/nsh/defconfig:86), so NuttX issues CMD24 for every sector. Nevertheless, `sdio_sendsetup()` unconditionally sets `BK7258_SDIO_DATA_MULTIBLOCK` at [bk7258_sdio.c:644](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_sdio.c:644). Beken’s available single-block CMD24 implementation explicitly programs bit 3 as zero at [sdcard.c:1392](/home/mi/vela_competition/bk_idk/middleware/driver/sdcard/sdcard.c:1392); its V2 path uses the multi-block engine only with CMD25. Pairing CMD24 with the multi-block host state can leave the controller expecting another block/stop condition or prevent a valid write-end event.

3. **High: `rwtest` is not recoverable across reset or power loss and may corrupt live filesystem data.**  
   The test selects the final physical sector at [sdnand_init_main.c:130](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/app/sdnand_init/sdnand_init_main.c:130), which can be inside an MBR partition and allocated to FAT data. It overwrites that sector four times beginning at [sdnand_init_main.c:140](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/app/sdnand_init/sdnand_init_main.c:140), while the sole backup exists only in stack RAM and is restored at [sdnand_init_main.c:162](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/app/sdnand_init/sdnand_init_main.c:162). A reset, crash, or power interruption during that interval permanently leaves a test pattern in an arbitrary filesystem sector. `--confirm` prevents accidental invocation but does not make the test safely recoverable.

4. **High: unmount, raw testing, and provisioning are not serialized as one storage transition.**  
   `bk7258_mmcsd_unmount()` releases `g_mmcsd_lock` at [bk7258_mmcsd.c:300](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/src/bk7258_mmcsd.c:300). The command then performs raw writes later at [sdnand_init_main.c:304](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/app/sdnand_init/sdnand_init_main.c:304), or formats at [sdnand_init_main.c:247](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/app/sdnand_init/sdnand_init_main.c:247), without retaining an exclusive operation lease. A concurrent `sdnand_init mount`, `periph_selftest`, or other caller can remount the volume between those steps. The MMCSD block lock only serializes individual I/O; it does not prevent raw writes underneath a mounted FAT filesystem.

**Other Findings**
5. **Medium: provisioning leaves a stale partition device and cached partition state.**  
   Existing MBR partitions are registered and cached at [bk7258_mmcsd.c:128](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/src/bk7258_mmcsd.c:128). Provisioning then formats `/dev/mmcsd0` as a whole-device FAT volume at [sdnand_init_main.c:243](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/app/sdnand_init/sdnand_init_main.c:243), but neither unregisters `/dev/mmcsd0p0` nor resets/reparses `g_partition_result`. Although provisioning explicitly mounts `/dev/mmcsd0` once, a later automatic mount follows [bk7258_mmcsd.c:74](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/src/bk7258_mmcsd.c:74) and can select the stale `/dev/mmcsd0p0` inode, producing a mount failure or exposing obsolete offsets.

6. **Medium: a failed remount is discarded and `rwtest` reports success.**  
   After the raw test, [sdnand_init_main.c:305](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/app/sdnand_init/sdnand_init_main.c:305) explicitly discards the result of `bk7258_mmcsd_mount(NULL)`. 7. **Medium: write status is sampled once even though Beken treats it as delayed.**  
   The ISR immediately rejects any write-end interrupt whose status is not already `ACCEPTED` at [bk7258_sdio.c:252](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_sdio.c:252). 8. **Medium: Kconfig permits configurations that cannot compile or cannot transfer data.**  
   `BK7258_SDIO` depends only on `MMCSD` at [chips/bk7258/Kconfig:36](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/Kconfig:36), but the implementation requires `MMCSD_SDIO`, `SDIO_BLOCKSETUP`, and LPWORK.    [bk7258_mmcsd.c:304](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/src/bk7258_mmcsd.c:304) and [bk7258_mmcsd.c:309](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/src/bk7258_mmcsd.c:309) read `g_mmcsd_mounted` and return a pointer to mutable `g_mount_source` without taking `g_mmcsd_lock`. `status` then reads those separately at [sdnand_init_main.c:282](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/app/sdnand_init/sdnand_init_main.c:282), so a concurrent unmount can produce inconsistent output or mutate the source string during `printf`.
